html:
Ibn Tumart was a Berber religious reformer from the Anti-Atlas mountains of Morocco who founded the Almohad movement. In 1121 his followers proclaimed him the Mahdi, the rightly guided one.

After studying in the East, he came home preaching the strict oneness of God, which gave the movement its name, al-muwahhidun. He attacked the Almoravid rulers of Marrakesh as lax and literal-minded. From the mountain village of Tinmel he organised the Masmuda tribes into a disciplined force.

He died around 1130. His disciple Abd al-Mumin took Marrakesh in 1147 and built the Almohad Caliphate, which ruled Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia and al-Andalus. The thinker Averroes served its court. Its rule in Spain was broken at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212.
sum: Ibn Tumart was a Berber religious reformer from the Anti-Atlas mountains of Morocco who founded the Almohad movement. In 1121 his followers proclaimed him the Mahdi, the rightly guided one.
